pull.title: KAFKA-21327: Replace JGit calls in build.gradle with the git CLI via providers.exec
pull.body:
Notes:
- JIRA ticket: KAFKA-21327
- Rationale: this is a prerequisite for KAFKA-21326 _(Enable Gradle configuration cache)_ ~which blocks upgrade to Gradle 10: KAFKA-20102 _Preparations for Gradle 10_~ _update_: see this [jira comment](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-21326?focusedCommentId=18129875&page=com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.issuetabpanels%3Acomment-tabpanel#comment-18129875)
- **drafted and smoke tested in a session with Claude Opus 5.5**
- **requires more manual (human) testing; testing steps will be added ASAP**


___


_Drafted with Claude, then reviewed and edited._

:x: **Pitfall**: 
- `build.gradle` opens the repository with JGit at configuration time to compute the `commit id` and the `RAT excludes`
- With the configuration cache enabled, Git.open starts external processes (`git --version`, `git config --system ...`) that Gradle cannot track, so it reports configuration cache problems and fails the build by default.

:bulb: **Solution**: 
- Use providers.exec to run `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git ls-files --others --directory` instead. Gradle tracks their output as configuration inputs, so a new commit or a new untracked file correctly invalidates the cache. 
- The RAT exclude set is unchanged: on a working tree, JGit's clean().setDryRun(true) output matches `git ls-files --others --directory` exactly.
- `.git` is now checked with `exists()` instead of `isDirectory()`, so builds in a git worktree (where .git is a file) also get the real commit id and run RAT.

This also removes an implicit dependency: since KAFKA-21086 the `org.eclipse.jgit` import in `build.gradle` relied on JGit being on the build script classpath transitively via the Spotless plugin; related PR :arrow_down: 
- #23450

**Note: `:generator` submodule keeps its own JGit dependency (fetched from `gradle/dependencies.gradle`).**

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

build.gradle opened the repository with JGit at configuration time to
compute the commit id and the RAT excludes. With the configuration cache
enabled, Git.open starts external processes (`git --version`,

`git ls-files --others --directory` instead. Gradle tracks their output
as configuration inputs, so a new commit or a new untracked file
correctly invalidates the cache. The RAT exclude set is unchanged: on a
working tree, JGit's clean().setDryRun(true) output matches
`git ls-files --others --directory` exactly.

This also removes an implicit dependency: since KAFKA-21086 the
org.eclipse.jgit import in build.gradle relied on JGit being on the
build script classpath transitively via the Spotless plugin (:generator
keeps its own JGit dependency).

.git is now checked with exists() instead of isDirectory(), so builds in
a git worktree (where .git is a file) also get the real commit id and
run RAT.
